headline: A customer's AI agent vetted a vendor before buying, leading to site changes
summary: A software vendor discovered an AI agent performed due diligence on their site before a customer made a purchase, highlighting critical gaps in their machine-readable web presence. This led to immediate site improvements.
details: A software vendor selling self-hosted business apps encountered a new kind of customer interaction: an AI agent. This agent spent two hours vetting their site before the human buyer completed an 11-second purchase, revealing how AI is changing online transactions.

The AI agent, identified by its User-Agent, fetched specific URLs like /bundle, /contact, /pricing, and /product. Each of these returned a 404 error, indicating missing pages that a human might intuitively look for.

The vendor realized that the 'machine-readable surface' of their store is now load-bearing. While a human might infer information, an AI agent relies on direct access to pages like /terms, /refunds, /contact, /support, and /sitemap.xml.

Following the agent's visit, the vendor immediately created the missing pages for /contact, /pricing, /plans, and /product, ensuring they returned 200 OK responses. Eighteen new tests were added to cover these routes.

This incident underscores the importance of anticipating how AI agents will interact with websites. Vendors should check their 404 logs for common guessed addresses like /docs or /status, as these will form the basis of an AI's report to its owner.
